deckSubtitle: Workstream 5 capstone: 2-question topology decision tree, side-by-side Well-Architected comparison matrix, 1,000-tenant FinOps TCO model, and 3-stage elastic tenant tier lifecycle
tldr: Two Architectural Questions Select Your Pattern: First evaluate whether 100% of tenants legally require dedicated cloud projects (Pattern B); second evaluate whether you sell one uniform tier (Pattern A) or multiple tiers (Pattern C).
One 80% Reusable 5-Hop Codebase: Engineering writes the 5-hop ADK security and governance pipeline once; Patterns A, B, and C merely parameterize the surrounding Google Cloud isolation boundary.
The Multi-Tenant Agentic Triad: Sustainable enterprise AI platforms balance three interdependent pillars—Zero-Trust Cryptographic Security, Predictable Unit Economics, and Zero-PII FinOps Chargeback.

Proven 1,000-Tenant Portfolio Economics: Across 950 Standard and 50 Enterprise tenants, Pattern C reduces Gemini 2.5 Pro input token spend by 84.7%, lowers total cloud TCO by 74% vs. all-siloed, and maintains a 99.99% SLA.

Elastic 3-Stage Tenant Tier Lifecycle: Onboard commercial tenants in <50ms into Pattern A (120 RPM Pool), promote expanding enterprises live into Pattern C PSC spokes (0ms lag, 0 dropped turns), and enforce <60s HTTP 423 CMEK kill-switches in Pattern B silos.

sections.heading: Use cases — 2-Question Topology Selector, Competing Tenant Profiles & Unified Google Cloud Stack
bullets: Decision Gate 1 (Universal Regulatory Sovereignty Mandate): Do 100% of your customers legally require dedicated GCP projects, VPC Service Controls, IAM PAB, and customer-revocable CMEK kill-switches? If YES, standardize on Pattern B (600 RPM Silo).

Decision Gate 2 (Single-Tier vs. Multi-Tier SaaS Packaging): If not all customers require physical silos, choose Pattern A (120 RPM Pool shared pool, 90% prefix cache) for one uniform commercial tier, or Pattern C (74% TCO savings) for multi-tier portfolios.

Competing Tenant Profiles (FinVault Bank vs. RetailStream Corp): Co-host RetailStream in the 120 RPM Pool Standard pool (Entra ID, 4k cap, 120 RPM) and isolate FinVault in an 600 RPM Silo Enterprise spoke/silo (Workspace, 8k cap, 600 RPM, Agent Alpha, CMEK).

One 80% Reusable 5-Hop Google Cloud Stack: Cloud Armor, IAP OBO/DPoP, Agent Engine Registry, Memorystore Valkey, Gemini 2.5 Pro / Gemma 3, Model Armor, Cloud DLP, AlloyDB RLS/CMEK, and BigQuery OTel power all three patterns without code forks.

sections.heading: Design considerations — Multi-Tenant Agentic Triad (Security, FinOps & OTel)
bullets: Triad Pillar 1 — Zero-Trust Cryptographic Tenant Security: Enforces non-bypassable identity, tool discovery, memory namespace, prompt safety, and SQL RLS boundaries so tenant assets never commingle.

Triad Pillar 2 — Predictable Unit Economics & Quota Bulkheads: Combines 90% Gemini 2.5 Pro shared prefix caching discounts with Memorystore for Valkey RPM rate limiters and per-tier thinking token caps.

Triad Pillar 3 — Privacy-Safe FinOps Chargeback Telemetry: Streams zero-PII OpenTelemetry spans (`tenant_id`, `cached_tokens`, `thinking_tokens`, `silo_cmek_verify_ms`) into BigQuery for 3-model billing.
1,000-Tenant Portfolio Financial Proof: Across 950 Standard and 50 Enterprise tenants, the Agentic Triad saves 90% Cache Hit in cloud infrastructure and reduces per-turn LLM token costs by 84.7%.

sections.heading: Design considerations — Invariant 5-Hop Pipeline Across All Three Patterns

pipelineSteps.title: Perimeter WAF, Federated OIDC & DPoP Token Binding
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Strips unauthenticated X-Tenant-Id headers at the L7 load balancer, verifies Google Workspace or Microsoft Entra ID OIDC JWTs, and exchanges credentials via RFC 8693 OBO.
pipelineSteps.invariant: Cryptographic Claim: tenant_id + tier + DPoP (RFC 9449 jkt)
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 401 on Spoofed Header or Replayed Bearer Token

pipelineSteps.title: Tenant-Scoped Agent & MCP Tool Catalog Filtering
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Evaluates the signed TenantSecurityContext against Agent Engine Registry metadata before LLM tool-binding, returning only shared platform tools and tenant-owned private agents.
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 403 Forbidden on Cross-Tenant Agent or MCP Discovery

pipelineSteps.title: Sandboxed ADK Execution, L1–L5 Memory & Quota Bulkheads
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Executes agent reasoning inside gVisor-isolated Cloud Run v2 / Agent Engine sandboxes, partitions L1–L5 Memory Bank namespaces, and enforces per-tenant RPM and thinking budgets.
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 429 on RPM Burst • HTTP 403 on Cross-Namespace Read

pipelineSteps.title: Bidirectional Model Armor Screening & Sensitive Data Redaction
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Screens ingress prompts and retrieved RAG chunks for prompt injection/jailbreaks, enforces tenant Natural Language Constraints (NLCs), and redacts egress PII/PCI/IBAN tokens.
pipelineSteps.invariant: Policy: inspectContent + deidentifyContent + Tenant NLC Rules
pipelineSteps.gate: HTTP 400 on Prompt Injection • HTTP 422 on NLC Policy Breach

pipelineSteps.title: Transactional Row-Level Security, CMEK & Zero-PII Telemetry
pipelineSteps.mechanism: Binds parameterized PostgreSQL session context (app.current_tenant_id) for mandatory Row-Level Security, verifies Cloud KMS CMEK liveness, and streams zero-PII OTel spans to BigQuery.
pipelineSteps.invariant: SQL: SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id • OTel Chargeback Ledger
pipelineSteps.gate: 0 Unauthorized Rows • HTTP 423 Locked on CMEK Revocation

bullets: Hop 1 — Edge WAF & Identity Binding: Cloud Armor and IAP/STS mint a DPoP-bound TenantSecurityContext across Pooled, Siloed, and Hybrid deployments.
Hop 2 — Registry Discovery Filtering: Vertex AI Agent Engine Registry filters shared and private agents by tenant visibility before prompt assembly.
Hop 3 — Sandboxed Runtime, Memory & Quotas: Enforces L1–L5 Memory Bank namespaces, Valkey RPM bulkheads, and 4k/8k thinking budgets (plus CMEK heartbeat in Silos).
Hop 4 — Bidirectional Model Armor & DLP: Blocks prompt injection (400) and semantic NLC violations (422) while masking egress IBAN/SWIFT/PAN PII.
Hop 5 — Transactional RLS, CMEK & FinOps: Enforces AlloyDB Row-Level Security or dedicated CMEK spoke storage and logs zero-PII OTel spans to BigQuery.

takeaways: Resolve Regulatory Mandates Before Product Packaging: Always evaluate whether compliance requires physical per-tenant projects (Gate 1 -> Pattern B) before choosing between single-tier (Pattern A) and multi-tier (Pattern C).
Standardize on One 5-Hop Security Pipeline Across All Tiers: Keep 80% of your Python ADK application code identical across Pooled, Siloed, and Hybrid environments.

Treat Pooled ($), Hybrid ($$), and Siloed ($$$) as One Continuous Platform: Use Firestore routing metadata and Private Service Connect to move tenants across tiers without changing URLs or rewriting agents.

Balance All Three Pillars of the Agentic Triad: Combining 5-hop zero-trust security, 90% prefix caching + Valkey bulkheads, and zero-PII BigQuery OTel chargeback protects both CISO compliance and CFO margins.

Gate Every Production Release on the 12-Point Forensic & 20-Test Simulation Suite: Run `python3 -B scripts/run_deep_forensic_audit.py` to certify code, diagrams, Terraform blueprints, and live GCP resources.

slideSpeakerNotes.title: Act II (Level 4 Zoom) — Wire-Level Payload & Cryptographic Context Transformation
slideSpeakerNotes.whyHere: This slide completes our four-level architectural zoom in Act II—taking us from the step-by-step timeline on Slide 6 right inside the JSON message envelope traveling across the wire.
